items.text: Same `forEach(async ...)` issue exists in another reschedule file - surrounding try/catch no longer catches getCalendar failures, resulting in unlogged unhandled rejections that can crash the process

Line 26 in getVideoAdapters can reject, and while createMeeting is protected by try/catch with fallback, updateMeeting, deleteMeeting, and getBusyVideoTimes all await getVideoAdapters without error handling - a single broken provider will fail all these paths

forEach with async callback in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts creates fire-and-forget promises - the email may be sent before deletions complete and function may return true before all operations finish

forEach(async ...) isn't awaited in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, so calendar/video deletions can run after the function continues and failures won't be caught by the outer try/catch, potentially leaving orphaned external events/meetings

In vital/lib/reschedule.ts, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(...)` changed to `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar` inside, causing getCalendar failures to become unlogged unhandled promise rejections instead of being caught by surrounding try/catch. Can crash process under Node's default --unhandled-rejections=throw. Fix: use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or for...of with await inside the try
Calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget with no error handling because the surrounding try/catch cannot catch errors from async forEach callbacks

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts lines 589-596, app resolution and PaymentService instantiation happen outside the try-catch block - if either fails, the error bypasses handleRefundError leaving refund flow incomplete
Same `forEach(async ...)` issue in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: getCalendar errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.

App store entries use `import("./x")` in object literal which loads all 28 app packages immediately on first import rather than lazily - async imports run when the literal is evaluated, not when keys are accessed. Fix: use thunks `key: () => import("./x")` with `await appStore[key]?.()` at call sites
sendRequestRescheduleEmail executes before deletions complete due to forEach not awaiting async callbacks
Handle failures from getCalendar - awaited call is not wrapped in error handling so rejected import inside async callback will go uncaught (packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:128)

getCalendarCredentials calls getCalendar without await, so exported return items now have `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of resolved value. Future callers reading item.calendar directly get a truthy Promise that passes `if (!calendar)` checks incorrectly

Developer docs still instruct adding a static import to packages/app-store/index.ts; the convention is now `appname: import("./appname")`, so contributors following the docs reintroduce the eager pattern.

await getCalendar(...) is inside an un-awaited forEach(async ...) in handleCancelBooking.ts, so Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) can run before recurring-series deletes have been enqueued
Race condition where the function proceeds (e.g., sending reschedule emails) before external events are actually removed due to unawaited forEach
Leftover comment `// example: import("./example")` points at ./example while the folder is _example; dead either way.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts lines 458-470, forEach with async callback causes race condition - handler can reach Promise.all before delete operations start, and line 467 pushes resolved value instead of promise itself breaking promise tracking
Wrap the awaited appStore lookup in error handling so a failed dynamic import doesn't throw out of deletePayment without a controlled response (packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts:16)
Handle errors from the awaited appStore import so a failed dynamic import doesn't surface as an unhandled rejection (packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:15)
Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
Using forEach(async ...) in 4 locations causes returned promises to be silently discarded since Array.prototype.forEach does not await async callbacks

Dynamic imports in packages/app-store/index.ts are still eager - each import() runs when module is evaluated, so importing appStore kicks off every provider load immediately instead of true on-demand loading

getCalendar unawaited returns Promise object - In getCalendarCredentials at line 28, getCalendar(credential) is now async but is not awaited. The calendar field in returned objects is a Promise (always truthy) instead of Calendar | null, creating a fragile implicit contract where callers must know to await the field. Any caller checking if (!calendar) will never see null since a Promise is truthy.

appStore values are `import("./x")` expressions evaluated when the object literal is built, so all ~28 app packages still load on first import of @calcom/app-store; the change is async but not lazy, and every caller paid async churn for no load-time gain. Fix: use thunks `key: () => import("./x")` and `await appStore[key]?.()` at call sites.

`forEach((ref) => ...)` became `forEach(async (ref) => { await getCalendar(...) })` inside try/catch; getCalendar/CalendarService constructor throws now escape the catch as unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Fix: use `await Promise.all(map(async ...))` or for...of with await inside the try.

forEach does not await async callbacks so errors from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting will bypass surrounding try/catch - use await Promise.all or for...of loop (packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125)

await runs inside a forEach(async …) which isn't awaited - use a for…of loop or Promise.all so calendar deletions finish and errors surface before the handler continues (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:243)

forEach async callback drops errors - In 4 locations, forEach callbacks were changed to async to accommodate the now-async getCalendar, but Array.forEach() does not await async callbacks. The async callbacks fire as dangling promises — errors become unhandled rejections, wrapping try/catch blocks cannot catch them, and subsequent code runs before deletions complete, causing calendar events and meetings to silently fail to be deleted.

Pre-existing issue: `forEach(async ...)` pushes into apiDeletes after an await, so those deletes race the later Promise.all and may never be awaited; the patch adds another await (getCalendar) inside this callback.

requestReschedule now uses `forEach(async ...)` around `await getCalendar`; a getCalendar throw previously failed the mutation before emails/DB updates, now the mutation proceeds and the error is a detached unhandled rejection.
Errors from async forEach callbacks become unhandled promise rejections which can crash Node.js process

The awaited getCalendar call has no error handling inside the async callback - if it rejects the error becomes unhandled because callback promise isn't awaited (packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:128)
The for loop in getVideoAdapters serializes adapter loads, reducing performance compared to parallel loading
No tests added or updated for the changed async contract of getCalendar/getVideoAdapters/appStore lookups.
apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) pushes the resolved value (not a promise), so it won't actually be awaited downstream in the Promise.all
The calendar property in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts now holds Promise<Calendar | null> but property name doesn't indicate async nature - may confuse consumers expecting resolved Calendar object

forEach with async callback in packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts creates fire-and-forget promises that won't be awaited or caught - errors in getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting will be silently swallowed

Avoid async callbacks in forEach - deletions are not awaited so cancellation work can continue or fail after the function moves on - use Promise.all or for...of loop (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553)

CONTRIBUTING requires a full production build and yarn lint to pass; not verified, so TS narrowing on awaited module unions (`"lib" in calendarApp`) is unchecked by the compiler. Also eslint preset lacks no-floating-promises/no-misused-promises, so lint would not catch the forEach(async) issue.

In requestReschedule mutation, `forEach` became `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar`, causing synchronous getCalendar throws to become detached unhandled rejections. Mutation continues silently, sending emails and updating DB even when calendar operations fail
Handle errors from the awaited getCalendar call - rejected import will bubble out of createEvent without any recovery or logging (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:233)

forEach with async callback in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx creates fire-and-forget promises - errors won't propagate and sendRequestRescheduleEmail may execute before deletions complete
Wrap the awaited appStore lookup with error handling so a failed async import doesn't throw out of the cancellation flow (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:589)

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
Wrap the awaited appStore import in error handling so a failed async import doesn't throw past this function without context (packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts:26)

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) isn't awaited in bookings.tsx, so calendar/video deletions may still be in-flight or fail while the router continues to send reschedule email, leading to inconsistent external calendar/video state
bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) doesn't get awaited, and the surrounding try/catch won't catch async rejections from deleteEvent/deleteMeeting, so integration cleanup can fail silently

Wrap the awaited appStore import in error handling - dynamic imports can reject and without try/catch this will throw and interrupt the refund flow (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:967)

getCalendarCredentials now stores an un-awaited `Promise<Calendar|null>` in the `calendar` field; a future caller that forgets to await gets a truthy Promise, and discarded promises that reject are unhandled.

A failing app-module import now rejects at module evaluation with no handler attached until some request awaits that key, surfacing as an unhandledRejection (process exit under Node defaults) instead of a catchable import error.
Should use for...of or Promise.all with .map() instead of forEach with async callbacks (pattern already correctly applied at handleCancelBooking.ts:474-486 but missed in other locations)

forEach doesn't await async callbacks so calendar/video deletions run in background and errors won't be caught by surrounding try/catch - use Promise.all with map and await (packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125)
In handleCancelBooking.ts:458, apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) pushes the resolved value rather than a Promise, so Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) will not wait for the deletions

issues.claim: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, the booking-ref loop was changed to `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar` inside. The promises are not awaited, so getCalendar, deletion and import failures escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections. The function and the reschedule email can also proceed before the deletions complete.

In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was changed to `forEach(async ...)` with `await getCalendar` inside. The callback promises are not awaited, so getCalendar, deleteEvent and deleteMeeting failures bypass the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections or are silently lost.

In the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` around `await getCalendar` is not awaited. Calendar/video deletions run detached, their errors become unhandled rejections, and the mutation continues to send reschedule emails and update the DB before or despite deletion failures.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, `await getCalendar(...)` sits inside an un-awaited `forEach(async ...)`. As a result, `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` can run before the calendar/recurring-series deletes have been enqueued, and errors do not surface before the handler continues.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` pushes the resolved value rather than a promise. The later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` therefore does not wait for those deletions.

Across the changed locations, forEach callbacks were made async to accommodate the now-async getCalendar. Array.prototype.forEach does not await them, so the promises are discarded: errors escape surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections, and subsequent code such as sending reschedule emails runs before deletions complete.

updateMeeting, deleteMeeting and getBusyVideoTimes await getVideoAdapters without error handling, unlike createMeeting, so a rejection in getVideoAdapters from a single broken provider fails all these paths.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts around line 589, the awaited appStore lookup and PaymentService instantiation happen outside the try/catch. A failure there bypasses handleRefundError and throws out of the cancellation/refund flow.

In packages/app-store/index.ts, appStore values are `import("./x")` expressions evaluated when the object literal is built. Importing appStore therefore loads all app packages immediately rather than lazily on key access.
Developer docs still instruct adding a static import to packages/app-store/index.ts, while the convention is now `appname: import("./appname")`.

getCalendarCredentials in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts calls the now-async getCalendar without await. The returned `calendar` field is therefore a `Promise<Calendar | null>`, which is always truthy and so passes `if (!calendar)` checks, and discarded promises that reject are unhandled.
A leftover comment `// example: import("./example")` references ./example while the folder is named _example.
In packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts:16, the awaited appStore lookup has no error handling, so a failed dynamic import throws out of deletePayment.
In packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:15, the awaited appStore import has no error handling, so a failed dynamic import surfaces as an unhandled rejection.
An await of an import has no try/catch around it to handle import failures.
The for loop in getVideoAdapters loads adapters serially rather than in parallel.
No tests were added or updated for the changed async contract of getCalendar, getVideoAdapters and appStore lookups.

The production build and yarn lint required by CONTRIBUTING were not verified, so TS narrowing on awaited module unions is unchecked. The eslint preset lacks no-floating-promises/no-misused-promises, so lint would not catch forEach(async).
In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:233, the awaited getCalendar call in createEvent has no error handling, so a rejected import bubbles out without recovery or logging.
In packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts:26, the awaited appStore import has no error handling, so a failed import throws past the function without context.
In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:967, the awaited appStore import has no error handling, so a rejected dynamic import interrupts the refund flow.

A failing app-module import now rejects at module evaluation with no handler attached until a request awaits that key. It therefore surfaces as an unhandledRejection instead of a catchable import error.
